name: Prescribed-Prefix Attachment Bound
statement: For $\emptyset\ne I\subseteq C$, put $\rho(C,I)=\max(\{q(c,I):c\in C\setminus I\}\cup\{0\})$. Then $\max\{\sigma(C),\sigma(I)\}\leq\sigma(C;I)\leq\max\{\sigma(C),\sigma(I),\rho(C,I)\}$.
proof: The lower bounds follow by forgetting the prefix constraint and by restricting an admissible order to its initial segment. For the upper bound, take an optimal order of $C$, move $I$ to the front in an optimal internal order, and retain the relative order outside $I$. A minimal disagreement against the enlarged predecessor family $P\cup I$ is minimal against $P$ or against $I$, so its excess is bounded by the corresponding old step or by $q(c,I)$.
